findings.issue: SPEC-03 says 'every default range of all three reference sizes', but the sweep only asserts ranges.length > 0. If a reference size or most ranges went missing from DEFAULT_RANGES, the sweep would quietly cover less. The spec's figure of 90 ranges is also out of date: DEFAULT_RANGES now has 102. The loop covers all of them, so the behaviour is still tested correctly.
findings.fix: Add expect(Object.keys(DEFAULT_RANGES)).toHaveLength(3), or pin the current range count (102), so that the sweep's coverage is asserted. Optionally correct '90' in the spec's A-1 and edge-case text when it is next edited.

summary: The change matches the spec. scaledWidthPct returns early with o from 100 hands, and the arithmetic below 100 hands is unchanged. fillTemplate was moved unchanged into explanations.ts. basisText now calls fillTemplate(OBSERVED_BASIS, ...). explain.ts imports fillTemplate and re-exports it, the unused CONCEPTS import is gone, and the river-bet phrase swap is left alone (A-2). Mutation checks: putting back the Math.min form makes AC#1 and the SPEC-03 unit test fail, and putting back OBSERVED_BASIS.replace('{hands}', ...) makes the SPEC-04 unit test fail. In a re-run, the default playtest SHA is f6c8d172...7cbc with 0 invariant violations, matching the spec. The build log records both SHA pairs. The --check-advice run was not repeated because it takes about 2.5 minutes. All gates pass. The line count is 209 against a budget of 140, which is a warning only: most of it is the acceptance helpers the spec asked to be copied. One MINOR finding: the SPEC-03 sweep does not pin how many ranges it covers. There are no BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
